args.subject: User Legal Inquiry
args.body: I'm in the middle of a legal matter and could use some clarity. It's a immigration status review case. I hired Michael Torres at Dowd Legal; we have a hearing at small claims court coming up. The timeline is We're in the early stages; our first hearing is next month.. The other side is the other parent in the custody case. This is in Hennepin County, Minnesota. My status has changed and I need to understand the implications. What should I ask my attorney about how to protect my interests in the settlement talks? I want to be prepared for the legal process.

User: I'm in the middle of a legal matter and could use some clarity. It's a immigration status review case. I hired Michael Torres at Dowd Legal; we have a hearing at small claims court coming up. The timeline is We're in the early stages; our first hearing is next month.. The other side is the other parent in the custody case. This is in Hennepin County, Minnesota. My status has changed and I need to understand the implications. What should I ask my attorney about how to protect my interests in the settle

ment talks? I want to be prepared for the legal process.
Assistant: Thanks — useful detail. I’ve made a note of this and can help you get ready. Below is a focused, practical checklist of the questions to ask your attorney (and things to bring to the meeting/hearing), plus short negotiation and courtroom-prep tips. If you want, I can also draft an email or message you can send to Michael Torres with these points.

Important first clarification to confirm with your attorney
- Confirm the correct court and ca

se type. Small claims courts usually handle monetary disputes; custody matters are handled in family/divorce court. Ask Michael to confirm which court and judge will hear your matter and why this is in small claims (if that’s what you were told).

Questions to ask your attorney about settlement and protecting your interests
- Scope & strategy
  - What is our overall strategy for settlement vs. trial?
  - What are the realistic best and worst outcomes if we go to hearing?
  - Should we try mediation, and if

so, when?
- Immigration consequences
  - Could any settlement terms, admissions, or findings in this case affect my immigration status, removability, or applications (current or future)?
  - Are there particular phrases, admissions, or concessions I should avoid in written or spoken agreements?
  - Should I consult or retain an immigration attorney to review any settlement before I sign?
- Custody and parental rights
  - How will proposed custody/parenting-time terms affect my parental rights and future cus

tody modifications?
  - Will child support or financial terms be enforceable across jurisdictions if needed?
- Criminal or domestic-violence implications
  - Will admitting fault, entering into an agreement, or certain parenting-time arrangements trigger criminal, protective-order, or immigration consequences?
  - If there are safety concerns, what protective language or orders should we seek?
- Confidentiality, sealing, and public record
  - Will settlement terms be part of the public court record? Can the

y be sealed or kept confidential?
  - If confidentiality is important, how should we draft the release/settlement language?
- Payment and enforcement terms
  - If money will change hands (support, lump sum, etc.), what’s the safest way to structure payments to protect me and show compliance?
  - What enforcement mechanisms should we include (e.g., wage garnishment, contempt language)?
- Admissions and release language
  - Can we draft the agreement to resolve the dispute without admissions of wrongdoing?

- Are there standard “no admission of liability” clauses you recommend?
- Timing and postponement
  - If my immigration status is changing, is it advisable to seek a continuance until immigration issues are clearer?
  - Will delaying settlement or hearings change my immigration risk?
- Costs, fees, and representation scope
  - What are your fees for settlement negotiations vs. trial?
  - Are you handling only the custody/small-claims side or also the immigration consequences? If not, can you coordinate with

an immigration lawyer?
- Evidence and witnesses
  - What evidence will we need for the hearing and to support settlement positions?
  - Which witnesses are critical, and will bringing them to a hearing hurt my immigration position?

Documents and evidence to bring to your attorney/hearing
- All immigration documents: passports, I-94, visa, work authorization (EAD), receipt notices, approval notices, pending applications, any USCIS/immigration correspondence.
- Court documents: petitions, prior orders, hear

ing notices, filings from both sides.
- Communications between parties: texts, emails, social-media messages relevant to custody/dispute.
- Financial records: paystubs, bank statements, proof of child-related expenses.
- Police reports, protective orders, medical records (if applicable).
- Calendar/timeline of important events (dates of incidents, filings, hearings).
- Any witness contact info and brief summaries of what they can attest to.

Settlement-drafting tips to minimize immigration risk
- Avoid writ

ten admissions of criminal conduct or abuse in settlement language; use neutral phrasing when possible.
- If payments are involved, consider structuring them as child support or specified reimbursements rather than lump-sum “settlement for damages” if your attorney advises that’s safer.
- Add explicit clauses that the settlement contains no admission of liability.
- Specify confidentiality/sealing if needed and request non-public filing or in-camera review where possible.
- Require attorney review and a sho

rt review period before signing so you can get immigration counsel input.

Hearing logistics — what to expect and ask
- Ask who will be present, the estimated length, and the judge assigned.
- Ask if evidence must be filed ahead of the hearing and by when.
- Ask whether witnesses will testify in person or by declaration, and how to introduce exhibits.
- Ask whether you should request an interpreter if needed, or request accommodations.
- Ask whether a continuance is available and how to request one.

Safety

and immediate priorities
- If there are safety or domestic-violence concerns, tell your attorney immediately; safety takes priority and may change strategy (protective orders, supervised exchanges, etc.).
- If you feel pressured to sign anything quickly, request time to have an immigration attorney review the terms.

Next steps I can help with
- Draft a concise list of questions to send to Michael Torres (I can draft an email or a one-page checklist).
- Draft a short message you can bring to the hearing or

keep on hand.
- Search your inbox for emails from Michael Torres or Dowd Legal and draft/send a message to him (if you want me to locate or contact him, tell me to search or to draft/send).

Would you like me to:
1) Draft an email you can send to Michael Torres with these questions? or
2) Search your inbox for Michael Torres / Dowd Legal emails and prepare a reply or draft?

Which would you prefer?
